message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the products in Products.txt, covering roughly the last 24 hours before 2026-06-24 15:42 IST. Relevant new or newly escalated items were found for Ubiquiti/UniFi, Python, OpenSSH, and ManageEngine. A Fortinet/FortiBleed item from June 23 was reviewed, but Fortinet states it is not a new vulnerability, so it is not counted as a fresh vulnerability finding.

**Finding 1**

- Product: Ubiquiti / UniFi OS
- Issue: CVE-2026-34908, CVE-2026-34909, CVE-2026-34910
- Severity: Critical; each is listed with CVSS 10.0 by the CNA data shown in NVD
- Description: UniFi OS has an improper access control flaw, a path traversal flaw, and an improper input validation flaw that can be chained to make unauthorized system changes, access files, and execute command injection.
- Relevance: Ubiquiti/UniFi is in the monitored product list. NVD shows these CVEs were added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-06-23 and the CISA SSVC status was updated to active exploitation.
- Sources: NVD CVE-2026-34908: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-34908; NVD CVE-2026-34909: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-34909; NVD CVE-2026-34910: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-34910; Ubiquiti Security Advisory Bulletin 064: https://community.ui.com/releases/Security-Advisory-Bulletin-064-064/84811c09-4cf4-42ab-bd61-cc994445963b

**Finding 2**

- Product: Python / CPython tarfile module
- Issue: CVE-2026-11972
- Severity: High; CVSS v4.0 base score 8.2 in the CVE/NVD data
- Description: Python's tarfile module may fail to handle EOF correctly when a tar archive is opened in streaming mode (`mode="r|"`), allowing a crafted archive to be parsed in an infinite loop and cause resource exhaustion.
- Relevance: Python is in the monitored product list. The CVE was newly published in the current monitoring window.
- Sources: NVD CVE-2026-11972: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-11972; CVE Record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11972

**Finding 3**

- Product: OpenSSH
- Issue: CVE-2026-55655
- Severity: Medium; CVSS 5.0 per Red Hat CNA data in NVD
- Description: A local unprivileged attacker on a Linux client host may hijack client-side X11 forwarding connections when X11 forwarding is enabled and a local UNIX-domain X socket is used. This can expose forwarded X11 traffic and may allow limited manipulation of the forwarded session.
- Relevance: OpenSSH is in the monitored product list. NVD received the CVE from Red Hat on 2026-06-23 within the monitoring window.
- Source: NVD CVE-2026-55655: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-55655

**Finding 4**

- Product: OpenSSH
- Issue: CVE-2026-55653
- Severity: Medium; CVSS 4.3 per Red Hat CNA data in NVD
- Description: A malicious SSH server may trigger a double-free condition in the Diffie-Hellman Group Exchange client path when the OpenSSH client processes attacker-controlled DH-GEX group parameters in FIPS mode, causing client-side denial of service.
- Relevance: OpenSSH is in the monitored product list. NVD received the CVE from Red Hat on 2026-06-23 within the monitoring window.
- Source: NVD CVE-2026-55653: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-55653

**Finding 5**

- Product: ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus, RecoveryManager Plus, M365 Manager Plus, and ADAudit Plus
- Issue: CVE-2026-11374
- Severity: Critical; CVSS 9.0 per ManageEngine CNA data in NVD
- Description: Predictable SSO tickets could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over accounts in affected ManageEngine products.
- Relevance: ManageEngine is in the monitored product list. NVD records the CVE as received from ManageEngine on 2026-06-23 and modified on 2026-06-24.
- Sources: ManageEngine advisory: https://www.manageengine.com/products/self-service-password/advisory/CVE-2026-11374.html; NVD CVE-2026-11374: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-11374

**Relevant Advisory Updates**

- PostgreSQL: Red Hat issued RHSA-2026:28143 on 2026-06-23 for PostgreSQL 16 packages covering CVE-2026-6478 and CVE-2026-6473. This is a fresh package advisory, but the underlying PostgreSQL CVEs were disclosed earlier, so it is not counted as a brand-new vulnerability disclosure. Source: https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026%3A28143
- Google Chrome: Google posted Chrome 149.0.7827.197 for Android on 2026-06-23 and says Android releases contain the same security fixes as corresponding desktop releases unless otherwise noted. The June 23 Android post itself does not list new CVEs, so it is noted but not counted as a newly disclosed vulnerability set. Source: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/

**Possible Matches Needing Review**

- Fortinet / FortiGate / FortiOS SSL-VPN: A June 23 K7 Labs post discussed the FortiBleed credential exposure campaign affecting Fortinet firewalls and VPN gateways. Fortinet's own June 19 PSIRT blog states this activity is not a new Fortinet vulnerability and is not related to a recent advisory. Review Fortinet exposure operationally, but do not treat this as a new CVE finding. Sources: https://labs.k7computing.com/index.php/security-advisory-fortibleed-credential-exposure-campaign-targeting-fortinet-firewalls-and-vpn-gateways/; https://www.fortinet.com/blog/psirt-blogs/analysis-of-reported-credential-compromise-of-fortigate-devices
- WordPress plugin Simple Basic Contact Form: CVE-2026-8172 is a plugin-specific reflected XSS issue. WordPress is monitored, but this plugin is not named in the monitored list; include only if present in the environment. Source: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-8172
- Style Dictionary in Node.js server applications: CVE-2026-54639 is a package/library issue rather than a Node.js runtime issue; include only if Style Dictionary is used in server-side workflows. Source: https://www.tenable.com/cve/newest

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for UniFi OS and ManageEngine deployments because the UniFi items are now marked actively exploited and the ManageEngine issue is critical account-takeover risk. Python tarfile exposure should be reviewed where untrusted tar archives are processed in streaming mode. OpenSSH items are medium severity and context dependent, but should be reviewed where X11 forwarding or FIPS-mode DH-GEX client paths are used.
